paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to take home. Some Greeks just wanted to see Jesus, and Jesus answered, "The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified." (John 12:23) Then He says it plainly: "unless a kernel of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains only a seed. But if it dies, it bears much fruit." (John 12:24) The way to much fruit goes through His death, and He walks into it on purpose: "it is for this purpose that I have come to this hour." (John 12:27)

And look at what that means for you. He says, "I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw everyone to Myself," (John 12:32) and the writer tells us this points to the kind of death He was going to die (John 12:33). EVERYONE, including those Greeks who only asked to see Him! I spent years in the back of a dark drawer, so hear me: being drawn out of the dark is the best news a stamper ever got.

So what do you do with it? Jesus says, "If anyone serves Me, he must follow Me," and promises that "the Father will honor him." (John 12:26) He also says, "While you have the Light, believe in the Light, so that you may become sons of light." (John 12:36) Don't leave it for later, baker. The Light is right here, so believe in it, follow it, and let it show you where you're going.
